text:
julia: FYI customer ACME reporting embed->indexing pipeline failures after last night's deploy. ~30% of batches are rejected: "Invalid vector dimension: expected 96 got 128" but some batches succeed. Attaching log snippets.

carla: Which embedding model/route are they hitting? Any recent schema or indexer config changes? pinging @anshul for infra.

julia: They're using rift-embed-v2-quant via /v1/embeddings (default batcher). No customer-side schema change. We did a staggered indexer deploy 2026-03-16 ~22:10 UTC.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: indexer-service v3.14 deployed at 2026-03-16T22:09:58Z by carla

anshul: Looking at indexer logs — I see a split fleet: some workers still advertising vector_table_schema=legacy96. Canary rollback on a subset left old nodes in the pool. Those nodes accept 96-dim vectors and reject 128-dim ones. Repro quick test: POST two embeddings (one 96-d, one 128-d) to same route -> 96 accepted on old node, 128 rejected with the error above.

carla: Huh. The embeddings pipeline should normalize to 128. Could quantization or a legacy postproc be collapsing dims? @julia can you share request_ids for failing writes and raw payload bases?

julia: Sending sample request_ids: req_acme_20260316_028 (failed), req_acme_20260316_029 (accepted). Example failing payload snippet:
```
POST /v1/index HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "id": "req_acme_20260316_028",
  "vector": [0.012, -0.34, ... /* 128 floats */],
  "meta": {"customer": "acme"}
}
```
Response: 400 Invalid vector dimension: expected 96 got 128

mike: (ACME) We saw many 4xxs and partial success. Ingestion throughput dropped because our client retried and hit rate limits (429). Any risk of lost docs? We also noticed a billing jump from retry storms.

carla: Short answers: rejected vectors were not written (no silent loss). We'll identify affected shards and run backfill for failed request_ids. Plan: 1) detect shards reporting legacy schema, 2) drain writes to those shards, 3) roll them to schema v2, 4) backfill the rejected vectors from the retry logs/backoff queue. ETA ~4h once migration window opens.

anshul: Immediate mitigations: a) Route ACME traffic to the up-to-date indexer pool (avoid old nodes) — low-risk, ETA ~20m. b) As a last resort, enable a compatibility shim that truncates 128->96 on-the-fly — avoids 400s but degrades quality (not preferred). Also adding metric alert: mixed_dim_accept_rate > 5% on a route -> page.

julia: Customer agreed to route swap. I'll coordinate the DNS/route change and let billing know about retry-related spikes so they can credit any obvious double-bills.

carla: I'll own the indexer fleet rollout and backfill runbook. Runbook checklist (short):
- list affected nodes/shards (query /fleet/shards?schema=legacy96)
- pause writes to affected shards (route-level hold)
- deploy indexer v3.14 hotfix to remaining old nodes
- run backfill job with throttling: --rate=200/s --verify-checksum
- monitor customer ingest successes and embedding-match quality on sample set

carla: Posting follow-up in 15m with exact shard list and scheduled migration window. :thumbsup:

anshul: I'll also add a short-term log-parsing job to surface any other customers hitting mixed-dim errors in last 72h. :eyes:

julia: Thanks — marking this P1 for support escalation and ops handoff. I'll update ticket and close loop with ACME once routing done.
